These layers are perpetually stressed by unseen forces, causing the rock structure to constantly fail. Slow, creeping tectonic movement initiates subtle shearing motions, causing adjacent bands of color to slip and resist each other. Visible stress lines appear first, widening into faults where larger segments break and detach. The movement is continuous, resulting in the slow accumulation of fine, crumbled material filling the gaps and making the entire landscape appear unstable and eternally reforming.
